dataset: GaitRec -- a large-scale ground reaction force dataset of healthy and impaired gait
citation: Horsak B, Slijepcevic D, Raberger AM, Schwab C, Worisch M, Zeppelzauer M. GaitRec, a large-scale ground reaction force dataset of healthy and impaired gait. Scientific Data 2020;7:143. doi:10.1038/s41597-020-0481-z.
record_used: Processed vertical GRF (F_V_PRO), time-normalised to 101 points (0-100% stance) and body-weight-normalised, shod, standardised walking speed: healthy controls (CLASS_LABEL == HC, n=208 trials) vs knee-pathology patients (CLASS_LABEL == K, n=499 trials). The derived quantity is each trial's vGRF dynamic range = loading peak minus mid-stance trough.
pipeline: control.rds / patient.rds (vGRF waveforms) -> PhysioMoCap::grfLandmarks (loading peak, mid-stance trough, push-off peak; certified in the sibling gait-grf-gaitrec case) -> dynamic range = peak1 - trough, per trial. The two-element list (control, patient) -> PhysioAnalysis::twoSampleTTest (Welch). The benchmark reference re-computes the Welch t-test with scipy.stats.ttest_ind(equal_var=False) AND base R t.test, and reports the control/patient ratio. Deterministic.
note: This REUSES the certified twoSampleTTest op (validated bit-for-bit against scipy.stats.ttest_ind and base R in the sibling age-group-sway-bds case) and the certified grfLandmarks op (validated in the sibling gait-grf-gaitrec case) -- it is a NEW FINDING (an inferential certification), not a new op. The Welch t reproduces BOTH scipy.stats.ttest_ind(equal_var=False) AND base R t.test bit-for-bit. Finding: healthy controls (n=208) have a much larger vertical-GRF dynamic range (double-hump depth) than knee-pathology patients (n=499) -- mean 0.367 vs 0.196 BW, a ratio of about 1.87, t=17.3 on 337 Welch df, p~2.8e-48. Pathological gait flattens the GRF double-hump (lower loading and push-off peaks, a raised mid-stance trough): the flattened, less dynamic loading of cautious, impaired gait. This turns the sibling case's descriptive landmark means into a certified inferential group difference. A cross-sectional cohort (association, not causation), one processed vGRF per trial, knee-pathology class only.
